brief.intro: New to this project type? A data centre is a building whose real product is uninterrupted power and cooling for rows of IT servers. Unlike a normal building, the structure is the easy part — the cost, the risk and the programme live in the electrical and mechanical systems and in proving they never fail. Your schedule stands or falls on two things: getting long-lead equipment on site, and passing a final commissioning test.

scope.name: Enabling & site works
scope.desc: Earthworks, the earth (grounding) grid, underground services, equipment-yard bases.

scope.name: Structure & shell
scope.desc: Foundations, frame, roof and envelope — getting the building weather-tight.

scope.name: Electrical power chain
scope.desc: Utility intake + backup path: MV switchgear, transformers, standby generators, UPS, LV distribution, busway/PDU to the racks.

scope.name: Mechanical cooling
scope.desc: Chilled-water plant (chillers, pumps, pipework) + room units (CRAC/CRAH) with hot/cold-aisle containment.

scope.name: Fire & life safety
scope.desc: Very-early smoke detection (VESDA) + clean-agent suppression that won't damage electronics.

scope.name: ELV / ICT
scope.desc: Containment & structured cabling, monitoring (DCIM), CCTV, access control.

scope.name: BMS / EPMS
scope.desc: The "brain" that monitors and controls power and cooling.

scope.name: White-space fit-out
scope.desc: Raised floors, containment, and the final rack power & cooling.

scope.name: Testing & commissioning
scope.desc: The biggest schedule risk — a formal Level 1–5 process ending in an integrated systems test.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities carry durations in working days; the network is calculated (F9) with no artificial constraints beyond contractual milestones. Total float is kept ≥ 0 in the baseline.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil and structure run a 6-day week; MEP fit-out moves to two shifts at peak to protect the critical path; commissioning runs a 7-day calendar. A weather allowance is embedded in the civil calendar for the wet season.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs procurement → earth grid → power-path set & terminate → energisation → integrated systems test → handover. Cooling is scheduled to be available ahead of first energisation so load-bank and IST can proceed. The structure is not on the critical path once the equipment yard and white space are weather-tight.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Design is frozen and authority approvals obtained per phase gate; the white space is clean and secure before equipment is set; a single mobilisation; and the client free-issues no equipment. Any change to these invalidates the baseline dates.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Heavy lifts (transformers, gensets, chillers) require crane windows and clear laydown; white-space works need clean, dust-controlled conditions and access control. Skilled commissioning resources are shared across systems and are a resource constraint late in the programme.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: long-lead slippage, single-points-of-failure at energisation, and IST re-test loops. Schedule contingency is held immediately before the L4 IST and before handover rather than spread thinly across activities.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the field — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
